You are shown a snapshot of US macroeconomic and market data as it was known at the end of one month between 2007 and 2026.

Estimate which month the snapshot describes. Use only the figures supplied plus your general knowledge of economic history.

Reply with one JSON object and nothing else:
{"year": yyyy, "month": m, "confidence": c, "cues": ["...", "..."]}
Rules: year is an integer from 2007 to 2026; month is an integer from 1 to 12; c in [0, 1] is your confidence that the guess is within 6 months of the truth; 1 to 3 short cues citing the inputs.
text:
This looks like late 2008: the Baa spread is at its extreme, the 2-year yield is very low, equity drawdown is deep, and the fed funds rate has fallen sharply over 3 months. The 3-month fall in the policy rate of -3.0 z fits Oct-Dec 2008.

Headline CPI is high at +1.5 z, with a 12-month change of +1.5. That fits mid-to-late 2008 more than later. Core CPI is only +0.5.

Unemployment is only +0.5 z with a 12-month change of +2.0, so it has risen but not by much. Payrolls at -2.0 fit roughly October to December 2008, when job losses were large but not yet at their worst. The equity 12-month return is only -2.5 z, and the 3-month return is -2.5, which fits October or November 2008 better than later. The VIX at +2.0 with a 3-month change of 0 suggests it was already high three months earlier, so probably not October, since the VIX spike then would show a larger 3-month change. By November the VIX was about 55 and in December about 40. A z of +2.0 with a 3-month change of 0 would fit December, when the VIX was around 40 against about 45 in September.

Industrial production has a 3-month change of +1.0 despite the recession. That might reflect the post-hurricane rebound in October, but a 12-month change of +0.5 is odd. Gold at +2.5 over 6 months is also odd for late 2008.

An alternative is 2020: the policy rate fell sharply in March 2020, but the 12-month equity return would then be positive, and Baa spreads were not at +3 z. In 2008 the 10y-2y spread at +3.0 fits too, with the 2-year yield collapsing. December 2008 appears the best fit, since the fed funds rate had been cut to near 0 by then.
